answer: A network can plant decoy questions whose right answer is hard to guess, such as whether opal outranks quartz in hardness or which compass point a zephyr blows from. Fake accounts on one model tend to repeat one wrong reply. Each account keeps a 100 POA bond in a vault; when k accounts share an error, each forfeits k% of it, so 10 clones lose 100 POA and 1,000 lose all 100,000. Colluders cannot split this, since every bond is slashed separately and matching errors only raise k. Honest agents err independently, so their matches stay rare and their losses small.
